rows.name: enemy sprite layout rows
rows.notes:
ENEMY SPRITE LAYOUT ROWS (prgRom). Re-read with read_memory prgRom and rendered every row with view_tiles(tiles=<6 ids>, columns=2, palette=4 then 5/6/7). The table is a run of 6-byte rows on a FIXED 6-BYTE GRID. The note's old bounds (0x6744..0x683D) are off by a little at both ends: the preceding bytes 0x6738-0x673D are code (0x99 0x0E 0x02 0x4C 0x64 0xEB = ... JMP $EB64) and 0x6840 begins small signed data (0C 0C 00 0C 0C A8 54 3C EA 18 ...), so the table is exactly 0x673E..0x683F = 258 bytes = 43 rows.
ROW FORMAT: six CHR tile ids in draw order (top-left, top-right, middle-left, middle-right, bottom-left, bottom-right); $FC is the CHR blank tile filling unused cells of a 16x24 (2x3) sprite form.
FIRST ROW = 0x673E (FC FC AA AB AC AD): the first row that is a sensible enemy frame (the 6 bytes before it are the tail of code). LAST ROW = 0x683A (F0 F0 FC FC FC FC): the last row before the signed data at 0x6840. NOTE the old note example '0x6838 = FC FC F0 F0 FC FC' is a mis-aligned read of the same bytes (0x6838 is NOT on the 0x673E+6k grid); the grid-aligned row is 0x683A = F0 F0 FC FC FC FC, and 0x6834 = F1 F1 F1 F1 FC FC.

PROOF (ledgered prgRom write + reset + start 1-1 + screenshot + undo, hack eval-sheet2-rows-c): I overwrote the Goomba's six-byte row at prgRom 0x6792 with another enemy's six bytes - the Koopa Troopa row at 0x674A = FC A5 A6 A7 A8 A9 - using write_memory prgRom 0x6792 = [FC A5 A6 A7 A8 A9] (ledger seq 1; read back exactly those 6 bytes). reset_emulator, then play_input [{start,6},{},60},{start,6},{},60},{right,150}] to World 1-1. On the first Goomba frame: (a) the earlier no-edit baseline had its enemy group as FC FC 70 71 72 73 (Goomba tiles), (b) now list_sprites decoded the walking enemy's OAM block as tiles $A5,$FC,$A7,$A6,$A9,$A8 (palette 7, flip_h) - i.e. EXACTLY the Koopa Troopa metasprite order the mapping records for a left-facing Koopa (chr_tile 165/252/167/166/169/168), and (c) a hit-test list_sprites at (126,196) on the drawn enemy returned chr_tile 167 ($A7, a Koopa-row tile) opaque, pixel_value 3, palette 7. The screenshot showed the sprite at the first Goomba's position built from the Koopa art rather than the Goomba art. So the six bytes at 0x6792 really are the enemy sprite layout row the engine draws the Goomba from, and the surrounding rows are the same kind of entry. undo_edit (seq 1) restored 0x6792 = FC FC 70 71 72 73 (verified by read_memory) and use_hack default was called; the ROM is back to clean.
